title: The Village Next to Paradise: a more specific household
summary: The French introduction identifies the family members and the father’s casual work. The English introduction describes the household more broadly.
facts: English: An unnamed family navigates life in a Somali village. | French: A single father supports his son through small jobs; his sister returns after divorce. | Reading use: Check whether a catalogue introduction tells readers who belongs to the household and how it earns income.
notes: The comparison concerns these two saved synopses. Unstated details may still be present in the film.

title: War Pony: the stated reason for earning money
summary: Both versions list the same money-making activities. French explicitly describes the need to make ends meet; English describes Bill’s wish to advance himself.
facts: Shared detail: Both list siphoning fuel, delivery work and breeding dogs. | Difference: The descriptions state his economic aim differently. | Reading use: Separate listed activities from the reason supplied for undertaking them.
notes: Neither introduction establishes the absence of financial pressure. No poverty score or editorial motive is inferred.

title: My Sunshine: location and coach details
summary: The French synopsis identifies Hokkaido. The English synopsis identifies the skating coach as Arakawa and gives him a championship background.
facts: Shared detail: A coach prepares Takuya and Sakura to skate together in a competition. | English detail: The island is described broadly; the coach is named and his previous success is stated. | French detail: The island is named; the coach’s name and championship background are unstated.
notes: Different levels of specificity are compatible. These details do not establish a translation mistake.

title: Dog on Trial: different details about the same case
summary: English states that Cosmos bit three people and risks being killed if his defence fails. French names Dariuch as the person requesting the lawyer’s help.
facts: Shared detail: A lawyer agrees to represent a dog in court. | English detail: The incident and possible consequence are specified. | French detail: The human client and his request are specified.
notes: Only the bounded introductions are compared; the film and the correctness of either account have not been checked.

title: Vingt Dieux: a same-information control
summary: Both introductions give the same central family obligation, need for income and proposed cheese-making prize.
facts: Family: Totone is 18 and becomes responsible for his seven-year-old sister. | Livelihood: He aims to win a prize by producing Comté. | Plan: Both versions specify a gold award and a €30,000 agricultural prize.
notes: This is a control within the three reviewed factual fields, not a claim that every wording nuance is identical.

title: Godland: where factual comparison stops
summary: Both introductions identify a Danish priest travelling to Iceland to build a church and take photographs. Their closing moral descriptions use different language.
facts: English ending: Departure from purpose and moral direction. | French ending: Exposure to temptation and sin. | Review decision: Keep the shared actions; leave the broader meaning unresolved.
notes: Different moral vocabulary alone does not prove a changed event, translation failure or difference in national values.

title: The Blue Caftan: shared relationships and work
summary: Both introductions describe Halim and Mina’s marriage, their caftan business, his concealed homosexuality, her illness and the arrival of an apprentice.
facts: Relationships: The same couple and personal circumstances are specified. | Livelihood: Both place the couple in a traditional clothing shop in Salé. | Trigger: Both connect illness and a new apprentice with disruption of the household’s balance.
notes: The control checks explicit information in these fields. It does not certify equivalence of tone or translation quality.
